doc.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

title: Pessimism about American culture and globalization
summary: Talk of the economic crisis, money as the only value, and people not wanting to know.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Well you’ve said a few other things, not only about the 70s, but this is a leap to present day, but you sound fairly pessimistic about American culture in general, and especially having an experience in Germany and how they support the arts. And I liked this one thing. I think you were talking about the United States. You say, “You can afford a lot of worthwhile things if you’re not trying to run the world.”

Yeah. But part of that running the world is actually part of, well the phenomenon that’s happening now in our society, one of the unfortunate results of globalization, is this current economic crisis that we’re in. And so even the phenomenon, the action of running the world so to speak is really connected to a value system that places value only on material things and money. So you have this really tiny number of people at the top,

people who control the banks internationally, and one of the reasons why running the world is very lucrative is because it takes money. And so that’s one of the unfortunate things. I think part of this too, thinking about the proactivity of the students that I hung out with in my college days, I think that’s one of the things that’s diminished over the years. I think ironically at a time when we’re probably closer to a really major global crisis than at any time since then, since that period in the 60s and 70s, it seems like people more and more, almost instinctively, just don’t want to know what’s going on. They don’t want to know about what’s happening.
It’s so ironic because everything is knowable.
I mean everything is gettable. But we don’t want to know.

Yeah. I was intrigued that just the other day I ran across a quote, Aldous Huxley said that — I can’t remember the exact words but it was to the effect that the unfortunate thing about the ignorance of most people is that it’s not simply the fact of not knowing, but it’s that they don’t want to know.
